findings.reason: by the item's own rule a section adding surface must name what it retires or merges, and §11 must either book the helper against a retirement or state why it is not counted—the supplied counts are all zero, so the bookkeeping is the only place the addition is visible.
findings.text: §11 states "§11 adds two pieces of surface, and each is booked against a retirement" and lists only `Route.selected` (offset by the retired `RouteThresholds.select_margin`) and the `arms` edge property (offset by the three retired SignalSource properties); the new cross-IDS cluster-expansion function in imas_codex/ids/candidates.py is a further public definition that neither appears in that accounting nor in the supplied counts (all zero), so the section violates the rule it applies to its other additions

findings.reason: the plan already names graph_ops.py as the owner and schedules the workers.py deletion and the three importer repoints, so the duplication is the plan's declared target rather than a missed one.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — candidate graph access is concentrated in imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py behind `read_candidates`/`select_candidates`/`write_candidates`/`clear_candidates`/`count_candidates_by_route`, each a one-query operation hiding the edge schema, the section/data_type derivation and the route bookkeeping; DD retrieval stays owned by `retrieve_candidates` in imas_codex/ids/candidates.py, and §8 states "DD retrieval has one owner".
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan is a consolidation exercise that names the owner to extend in each case: the two live `count_candidates_by_route` definitions (imas_codex/ids/graph_ops.py:653 added by edge-ownership; imas_codex/ids/workers.py:419 still present) are collapsed onto graph_ops.py with the three importers in imas_codex/cli/discover/__init__.py:84,:161,:280 repointed, and every SignalSource→IMASNode create/delete is moved into graph_ops.py (`write_mapping_binding`, `clear_mapping_bindings`).
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §11 adds a third, uncounted public definition in imas_codex/ids/candidates.py (the cluster-expansion entry point `candidate_worker` calls between `judge_candidates` and `route`) while its own accounting names only two.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names and reuses the machinery it builds on: `hybrid_dd_search` (imas_codex/graph/dd_search.py:97) and `related_dd_search` (:606) for §4/§11 retrieval, the unfilled `SearchHit.see_also` (imas_codex/search/search_strategy.py:165, consumed only at imas_codex/llm/search_formatters.py:1212), `call_decisions`/`acall_decisions`, `PipelineCost` (§10), and the generalised claim routines in imas_codex/discovery/base/claims.py; §11 calls `related_dd_search(..., relationship_types="cluster")` rather than rebuilding cross-IDS cluster expansion.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no section adds a forwarding layer over existing machinery without justification; §11's expansion orchestrates retrieval and a second judgment call (it cannot be folded into `retrieve_candidates`, which runs before any ranking exists) and reuses the `same_quantity` noul and `CandidateWriteError` rather than adding a parallel path.
